## 1. Architecture and Board Workspace lifecycle

Build **AI Kanban**, a polished, static, GitHub Pages-deployable browser workspace for durable human–AI work. It has no backend, server routes, serverless functions, Node.js runtime dependency, WebSocket service, or separately installed local service. Ship semantic HTML, modern CSS, and standards-based JavaScript ES modules; use relative asset URLs so `index.html` works at a repository subpath. Vendor a pinned SQLite WASM distribution and all required worker assets locally rather than relying on a mutable CDN.

The useful core must work without an AI provider: users organize work, edit plans, preserve activity and research memory, inspect versioned outputs, and create/import handoff packets. A selected Board Workspace folder is the local trust, portability, collaboration, and persistence boundary. Each workspace contains `board.sqlite`, a versioned manifest, managed agent bootstrap files, attachments, artifacts, exports, and private coordination records at documented relative paths. Treat all workspace content, including agent-created content, as untrusted data.

On first run, present exactly these honest paths: **Open Board Workspace**, **Create Board Workspace**, and **Try demo**. Open/Create must be initiated by a user gesture in a secure context; feature-detect `showDirectoryPicker()`, request read/write permission only through that gesture, and retain a `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` in IndexedDB only for recent-workspace reconnection. On return, query permission first and request again only after a user gesture. Demo mode is clearly labeled memory-only and never claims connected-folder durability.

Create a manifest containing workspace id, format and schema versions, primary state file, reserved directories, generated bootstrap paths, and fingerprints of application-owned generated files. Show active folder name, permission mode, dirty/saving/saved/conflict status, and time of the last successful durable write. Before Open, Create, reconnect, Try demo, or Close replaces dirty state, require successful save or explicit confirmation; cancellation leaves the current workspace unchanged. Close clears in-memory domain state. Provide explicit portable archive export/import for unsupported browsers and label it as import/download rather than connected autosave.

Use a dedicated SQLite Worker. The worker owns the only live browser SQLite connection and exposes a validated message-based repository API for create, open, snapshot/query, mutation, export, close, and health operations. Main-thread UI modules must use repository/service interfaces and must never access raw SQLite or issue raw queries. Keep CPU-heavy database, search, parsing, and transformation work off the main thread. In-memory SQLite, OPFS, IndexedDB, and caches are working state only; the workspace `board.sqlite` is canonical.

Serialize browser writes through one coalescing save queue. Every mutation marks the external database dirty; explicit Save flushes pending committed mutations immediately. Before whole-file replacement, compare the current revision and file fingerprint with the loaded base; unexpected external change aborts the write and enters reload or explicit conflict recovery. Preserve prior bytes until a replacement stream closes successfully. Failed/cancelled writes remain dirty and recoverable. Coordinate tabs with Web Locks where available and `BroadcastChannel`; only a lock holder writes, and a second tab is read-only unless it obtains the workspace lock. Document a practical workspace-size limit because saves export complete SQLite bytes.

The board has ordered default columns with stable ids: Inbox, Planning, In Progress, Review, Blocked, Done. Users may create, edit, archive, search, filter, reorder, and move cards. The Quick Start demo loads a bundled Personal Research board with recurring cards for a macroeconomic pulse, things to do with a four-year-old in São Paulo, family trips, a collaborative vacation planner, and age-appropriate activities. Define explicit scope boundaries: no hidden cloud sync, multi-user service, autonomous hosted agent, or secure persistent browser credential store.

## 2. SQLite schema and repository operations

Use SQLite rollback-journal mode, foreign keys, full synchronous durability, a bounded busy timeout, deterministic transactional migrations, stable text ids, UTC ISO 8601 timestamps with offsets, and integer ordering keys. Store `schema_version` and workspace revision/control metadata in a metadata table. Reject unsupported future schema versions without modifying input bytes; preserve original bytes before migration. Validate every worker message, import, and SQL parameter; use bound parameters only.

Define normalized tables and indexes for at least:

- `workspace_metadata`: workspace id, format/schema version, revision, primary-file fingerprint, control generation, control owner/holder, protocol version, migration metadata, and managed-file fingerprints.
- `boards` and `columns`: stable ids, names, descriptions, order keys, archived state, timestamps; seed the six default columns while allowing user customization.
- `cards`: id, board id, column id, ordering key, `kind` (`task`, `question`, `result`), title, Markdown description, priority enum `P0`–`P3`, assignee, human/AI attention state, status projection, latest turn/result references, last-change actor, created/updated/archived timestamps, and review acknowledgment state.
- `card_dependencies`, `card_tags`, `attachments`, and relative artifact references. Validate all paths as relative, reject absolute paths, `..`, symlink escapes, and paths outside the selected root.
- `plan_items`: card/turn ownership, stable id, text, explicit state, ordering, actor, timestamps, and completion metadata.
- `execution_turns`: immutable id, card id, monotonic display number, `queued`, `claimed`, `running`, `needs_input`, `review`, `complete`, `failed`, or `cancelled` status; trigger/requester, assigned actor, agent run id, idempotency key, parent instruction/card revision snapshot, checkpoint/final summary/error, queued/claimed/started/updated/completed timestamps, output lineage, and memory read/write lineage.
- `outputs` and `output_versions`: turn ownership, typed surface id, version, status, actor, provenance, content or content reference, artifact path, timestamps, supersession, approval, and comparison lineage.
- `decision_threads`, `decision_options`, `decision_feedback`, and explicit gate decisions for `briefing`, `exploring`, `needs_feedback`, `committed`, `deep_work`, `review`, and `accepted` phases.
- `research_memory`, `research_sources`, and `monitor_cycles`: topic-scoped fingerprint, normalized subject, claim/event summary, source URL/publisher, evidence date, first/last seen cycle, content hash, relevance, `current`/`updated`/`superseded`/`dismissed`/`uncertain` state, coverage ledger, omissions, report lineage, and user correction/pin/forget actions.
- append-only `activity_events`: stable id, semantic type, actor, target, timestamp, summary, structured payload, visibility, correlation/trace id, and redaction audit metadata.
- `handoff_packets`, `agent_questions`, `coordination_audit`, and idempotency records.

Index board/column order, card search/filter projections, active turns, event chronology, output history, dependencies, topic fingerprints, and coordination lookup. Use SQLite FTS only if bundled and deterministically supported; otherwise implement validated indexed search without degrading correctness.

Repository operations must expose typed domain methods rather than generic SQL: create/open/migrate workspace; list/query/search/filter board; create/edit/archive/restore cards; reorder/move card; manage plans/dependencies/attachments; create/claim/checkpoint/question/resume/complete/fail/cancel/requeue turns; create/version/approve/compare outputs; record activities; persist and query monitor memory; import/export handoff packets; inspect/repair workspace; and acquire/release/reclaim control. Every mutation returns an updated snapshot or precise change record and emits typed, user-actionable errors for corruption, migration, lock, conflict, permission, export, and validation failures.

Moving/reordering a card and its movement activity insertion must be one transaction. Completing/failing a turn, updating its card projection/workflow position, and recording final activity must be one transaction. At most one active turn per card exists by default. A queued claim verifies expected revision and idempotency atomically. Requeue creates a fresh turn id and display number, snapshots current instructions, links a prior successful turn, and never reopens or mutates the completed turn. Moving completed work back to Inbox requires a Run again confirmation and invokes this requeue behavior.

## 3. Human-agent coordination and skill protocol

Install and maintain an application-owned, versioned bootstrap in every connected workspace: root `AGENTS.md`, root `CLAUDE.md`, and canonical `.agents/skills/ai-kanban/` containing `SKILL.md`, a dependency-free Python 3 CLI, and thin POSIX shell and PowerShell launchers. Root files point to the one canonical skill; they must not duplicate its operating contract. Record generated paths, protocol version, and fingerprints in the manifest. On reopen, verify the entire bundle and offer Repair or Update when missing, stale, or inconsistent. Never silently overwrite user-created or user-edited bootstrap files: show a comparison and require confirmation, updating only recognized generated content or explicitly approved managed sections.

The skill uses Python standard library modules only (`sqlite3`, `argparse`, JSON, filesystem APIs) and exposes validated commands for status, preflight, heartbeat/identity registration, ready-work listing, atomic claim/release, typed mutations, checkpoints, artifact publication, structured questions/answers, yielding control, handoff/status inspection, and opt-in watch mode. Mutations require expected revision, control generation, actor, run id, and idempotency key. Preflight validates Python and required standard-library capabilities. If a supported runtime is absent, explain the exact trusted installation command and obtain approval before any machine change; never install silently or elevate privileges.

Use `.ai-kanban/coordination/` as a private mailbox containing a versioned human signal record and separate versioned state record per approved agent. Each actor writes only its own record; all actors may read them. Every record includes workspace id, protocol version, actor/holder id, monotonically increasing sequence/control generation, timestamp, requested state, and last observed durable revision. Safely replace records and ignore incomplete, stale, workspace-mismatched, or lower-generation records. Keep substantive questions, answers, progress, outputs, and audit history in SQLite; mailbox records are signals, not a second domain database.

Model single-writer control as `human`, `granting_agent`, `agent`, `reclaim_requested`, and `recovering`, with owner, holder id, generation, workspace revision, and bounded lease metadata. A generation is an epoch; every mutation verifies generation, holder, and expected revision immediately before writing. Handoff requires request and acknowledgement: the current writer commits or rolls back, closes its writable stream/connection, publishes its final revision, then acknowledges before the next writer acts. Human reclaim has priority: an agent completes or rolls back its short transaction, rejects later mutations, publishes `yielded`, and must reread and receive a fresh grant to resume. Lease expiry is recovery evidence, never permission to overwrite; forced recovery invalidates the generation, waits for database/journal stabilization, validates integrity, and explains risk.

For browser whole-file SQLite export and native skill access, the control protocol is authoritative. Browser grant flow: flush pending save, increment generation, persist grant in SQLite, close writable stream, publish grant signal, and become read-only. Agent mutation flow: read latest human signal, open a fresh connection, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, verify control/revision in SQLite and mailbox, apply mutation plus audit event, increment revision, commit and close, then publish committed revision. Never hold a transaction while reasoning, waiting, polling, using tools, or generating artifacts. The browser reloads only after a valid commit marker, waits for journal disappearance, runs integrity check, confirms announced revision, and preserves selection, scroll, open detail, and unsaved drafts; drafts conflict rather than silently overwrite.

After create/reopen, show a concise Start your agent step. Tell users to open a terminal in the Board Workspace and start Copilot CLI, Claude Code, or another compatible agent; do not fabricate an absolute path or `cd` command from a directory handle. Show Waiting for agent until a valid heartbeat, then calmly show identity, control state, current turn, and last heartbeat. If absent, provide copyable fallback instructions, bootstrap diagnostics, Repair agent setup, and retry. Generated instructions require the agent to read manifest and skill, preflight, register heartbeat, inspect/resume work, then poll with bounded backoff, atomically claim one ready turn, work, checkpoint, ask/complete/yield, and return to watching while its host remains alive. An empty queue is quiet, not exit. State plainly that a skill cannot keep a terminated host runtime alive, consume future output, or initiate model turns; where host support is absent, watch mode is observation plus honest manual-resume guidance.

## 4. Cards, decision loops, execution turns, memory, and output surfaces

Cards are operational, scannable workspaces. Their compact form prioritizes title, latest useful summary/result, priority, attention state, turn status, assignee, dependencies, and badges; detail provides editable metadata/description, plan, turns, memory, history, activity, provenance, questions, outputs, archive, and publishing actions. Support task/question/result presentation, pointer and keyboard movement, accessible drag preview/drop targets, inline actions that do not conflict with selection, and explicit persistence/undo or rollback feedback.

Every turn is a bounded, immutable execution attempt for durable card intent. Agents claim a specific turn, and all mutations/artifacts cite card and turn ids. Initial template placement never starts costly work automatically: expose an explicit Ready for agent state. A turn needing human input remains active and resumes after an answer; it does not create a new turn. Cancellation retains partial output, activity, and reason. The card projects current status, turn count, latest preview, and attention state but never replaces chronological turn history. Make latest successful result prominent with status, age, rich preview, and Open action; retain older dated versions in ordered History and support comparison with clear new/changed/unchanged/superseded/failed labels.

Outputs are typed, versioned surfaces rather than one generic text pane: text/Markdown, status, link, program, table, diff, image/media, file, log/terminal, form, and extensible custom types. Each surface records ownership, schema version, status (`draft`, `streaming`, `complete`, `failed`, `stale`, `superseded`, `approved`), source, timestamps, provenance, and actions. Render safely: Markdown is sanitized, programs show language/path/copy affordances, tables validate schema, diffs compare before/after, images provide alt text/zoom/download/provenance, forms validate submission, and failed/stale surfaces explain recovery. Applying content externally is explicit and auditable.

Implement the vacation decision loop as a reusable decision-thread pattern. In Inbox, a human edits candidate destinations, goals, exclusions, budget/effort bounds, preferences, criteria, and unknowns. Planning creates an exploratory turn that compares a bounded set of credible options, including fit, evidence, tradeoffs, uncertainty, practical constraints, and why alternatives differ. It asks focused questions and yields `needs_feedback` when consequential preferences are missing rather than guessing. Humans rank, shortlist, reject, restore, annotate, add options, and revise constraints through append-only feedback. Before each research pass, the agent summarizes its interpretation, cites the feedback round, updates affected comparisons only, and explains material ranking changes.

Deep research is gated by an explicit recorded human commitment: selected option, current constraints, and an action such as Research selected option deeply. Positive feedback alone never authorizes it. A confirmed move from Planning to In Progress may atomically complete exploration and queue a deep-work turn. The deep-turn snapshot includes selected option, constraints, unresolved questions, evidence, and relevant feedback, and does not reconsider rejected choices unless new evidence invalidates them. Deep work creates dated itineraries and decision-specific artifacts. Review foregrounds the latest proposal, assumptions, dated evidence, unresolved risks, and approve/revise controls. Acceptance preserves all exploration, feedback, superseded proposals, and turn history.

Recurring-monitor cards execute dated cycles with cadence and a defined lookback window. Before a cycle, read prior reports and inspectable durable topic memory; do not rely on hidden model-session memory. Distinguish new developments from evergreen context, recycled commentary, duplicate coverage, corrections, forecasts, claims, and speculation. Store source-backed memory fingerprints and coverage ledger entries; classify findings as new, materially updated, unchanged context, duplicate coverage, corrected, or no longer current, and cite prior memory/cycles for deltas. Update memory only from committed source-backed results. Users can inspect, search, correct, dismiss, pin, export, and explicitly forget memory; forgetting affects comparison context but not immutable reports. Each report includes run date, cadence, lookback, exact topic, mode, new since last run, still-important context, source coverage, and gaps; preserve every report as a dated version with latest preview and historical comparison.

Provider-neutral handoff exports a selected card as compact, versioned JSON and Markdown containing intent, context, plan, relevant activity, and requested response shape. Users may copy/download it and paste/select an import response packet. Validate an imported packet completely before previewing changes; require approval for plan, output, status, and activity changes, and preserve packet plus resulting activity for provenance. An optional replaceable `AIProviderAdapter` may use a session-memory-only credential. Before network send, show provider, endpoint, model, exact selected content, and purpose, then require confirmation. Network failure leaves workspace unchanged with a retryable draft. Never treat imported AI text/structured values as HTML or executable instructions.

## 5. Interface states and interactions

Design a calm, capable, trustworthy workspace, not an operations console. Use restrained navy, mineral teal, warm paper, and coral attention accents. Use violet/teal for unreviewed AI changes and amber for Needs you, always paired with icon and text; never rely on color alone. Keep raw database mechanics behind an About workspace panel. Provide strong visible focus, native accessible controls, semantic labels for icon-only buttons, high contrast, reduced-motion behavior, responsive desktop/mobile layouts down to 320 CSS pixels, and keyboard-complete board/card interactions.

Global actions are state-aware. Before activation show Open/Create/Try demo; when active show Save, New card, Agent control, AI handoff, and Workspace menu. Foreground Needs you, AI working, and AI updated counts without a global chat pane or operational-dashboard clutter. Show useful empty columns, loading states, first-run state, dirty/saving/saved state, permission-limited state, conflict state, unsupported-browser state, corrupt/recovery state, and actionable errors. Treat native `hidden` as authoritative; CSS must not reveal inactive content.

Card detail supports metadata and Markdown editing, plan management, turn inspection, output/memory/history/activity/provenance views, replies to structured agent questions, Run again, archive, and publishing polished result cards. Cards last changed by an agent carry a calm accessible cue until reviewed. Search/filter includes column, priority, assignee, attention, active turn, blocked state, card kind, and monitor/decision status. Reordering/movement supplies optimistic feedback, validates allowed transitions, gives a visible reason for invalid moves, and rolls back consistently on conflict. Provide accessible keyboard alternatives to drag-and-drop and retain focus context after updates.

The active-workspace header displays folder/permission/save status, search, attention filters, and agent state. The agent panel distinguishes Waiting for agent, connected heartbeat, granted control, agent working, reclaim requested, stale heartbeat, and unsupported/manual handoff. It must not imply that opening a folder connects an agent. Preserve active human form drafts across agent commits and offer merge/reload choices when fields conflict. External change detection surfaces what changed and never overwrites silently.

Include a quiet footer linking the source promplet, compiled implementation specification, and public tutorial so the live demo remains traceable to its intent and generation path.

## 6. Security, compatibility, and recovery

Keep all workspace bytes local unless a separately initiated feature shows exactly what will be sent and receives confirmation. Never upload workspace files for analytics, crash reporting, diagnostics, previews, or hidden synchronization. Do not execute workspace files, generated artifacts, imported packets, Markdown, or attachments merely because they are within the authorized folder. Sanitize rendered Markdown and isolate unsafe previews. Validate manifest versions, SQLite content, packet schemas, file names, MIME/type claims, relative paths, and all browser/agent message payloads.

Use least authority: access only the selected workspace root, never traverse outside it, do not modify/delete unrecognized files, track managed files in the manifest, and require explicit confirmation for destructive cleanup. Directory permission revocation, missing primary files, invalid manifests, unsupported future versions, corrupt SQLite, partial export, migration failure, stale lock, save conflict, journal stabilization failure, and agent protocol mismatch each require a specific explanatory recovery path. Preserve original bytes before migrations and provide export/download wherever feasible.

The browser is a static application and must make its limitations visible: no secure persistent secrets, background service, guaranteed continuous agent execution, backend coordination, server-side authorization, or protection against unrelated/malicious programs that ignore the cooperative workspace protocol. Browser-only provider credentials remain session memory only and never enter localStorage, IndexedDB, URLs, logs, analytics, or workspace files. External network activity is explicit, names destination/purpose/progress, and provides failure/retry handling.

Support Chromium connected-folder autosave when File System Access is available in a secure context. Else support archive import/export with honest terminology. Ensure graceful behavior for unsupported Web Locks, BroadcastChannel, Worker, WASM, and File System Access capabilities. Browser validation must finish without uncaught page errors or unexpected console errors/warnings, including static-host/offline behavior.

## 7. File tree, implementation sequence, and test matrix

Deliver the complete implementation under `outputs/implementations/ai-kanban-browser/`. Include at minimum:

```text
outputs/implementations/ai-kanban-browser/
  index.html
  README.md
  src/
    app.js
    state/ workspace-service.js file-lifecycle.js control-service.js
    db/ sqlite-worker.js sqlite-client.js migrations.js repository.js queries.js
    domain/ cards.js turns.js decisions.js outputs.js activity.js monitor.js handoff.js
    ui/ shell.js board.js card-detail.js dialogs.js agent-panel.js surfaces.js
    styles/ tokens.css app.css
  vendor/sqlite/                 # pinned JS/WASM assets and license notices
  public/demo-board/             # bundled Personal Research sample workspace
  workspace-templates/
    manifest.json
    AGENTS.md
    CLAUDE.md
    .agents/skills/ai-kanban/
      SKILL.md
      ai_kanban.py
      ai-kanban
      ai-kanban.ps1
  tests/
    unit/
    integration/
    e2e/
  scripts/
    serve-static.*
    test.*
  docs/
    workspace-format.md
    agent-protocol.md
    handoff-packet.md
    recovery.md
    public-tutorial.md
```

Implement in this sequence: establish static shell, relative deployment paths, design tokens, accessibility baseline, and feature detection; vendor and validate SQLite WASM Worker loading; define schema/migrations/repository contracts; implement workspace lifecycle and serialized conflict-aware file persistence; build board/card/turn/activity/output UI; implement decision threads and recurring-monitor memory; install/verify/repair agent bootstrap and Python skill; add control handoff, mailbox, native SQLite transaction rules, and agent panel; add provider-neutral handoff and optional confirmed adapter boundary; complete import/export, recovery, responsive refinement, docs, demo board, and GitHub Pages deployment checks.

README must state local development command, test command, canonical data boundary, browser support, workspace-size guidance, agent/runtime prerequisites, and known limitations. Document workspace format, migration/recovery behavior, protocol, handoff packet schema, and the distinction between connected autosave and archive mode.

Acceptance and verification must include deterministic unit, integration, Playwright, and manual/visual coverage for: new workspace creation; existing reopen; manifest validation; schema migration/rollback/future-version rejection; export/reimport equivalence; corrupt input; worker error propagation; save queue coalescing; explicit save; permission loss; external modification conflict; two-tab write arbitration; card CRUD/search/filter/archive; pointer and keyboard movement/reorder with transactional activity; invalid transition recovery; plan/dependency persistence; active-turn atomic claim; duplicate idempotency rejection; Run again and confirmed completed-to-Inbox requeue; question/resume; cancellation with partial outputs; latest-result projection/history/comparison; decision briefing, feedback, commitment gate, changed selection, review/acceptance/cancellation; monitor delta classification, coverage gaps, memory correction/pin/forget, report history; output renderers and safe Markdown; packet validation/preview/approval/provenance; bootstrap create/reopen/repair/update and edited-file protection; valid/invalid heartbeat; handoff both directions; reclaim during agent work; stale generation/revision conflicts; duplicate claims; crash points before/after commit; journal stabilization; watcher restart/cancellation; unsupported hosts; agent termination honesty; narrow 320px layouts; reduced motion; keyboard and screen-reader checks; offline/static GitHub Pages subpath loading; and no uncaught browser or unexpected console errors/warnings.

The completed result is implementation-ready: requirements are concrete, all persisted fields and transitions are testable, lifecycle/recovery behavior is explicit, and the deliverable can be built without asking basic product-shape questions.
